faq.question: How much does it cost?
faq.answer: PLN 59 per month after the first 30 days. You test everything free for a month — full app, no limits. Cancel in account settings, no phone call needed.

faq.question: Do I need a card to start?
faq.answer: No. Sign up without a card and use the full app free for 30 days. You only pay (PLN 59/month) if you choose to continue after the trial.

faq.question: What's actually in the app?
faq.answer: Guest list with RSVP, budget, table plan with seating rules, tasks, vendor contacts and PDF export (floor plan, place cards). One shared account for the couple.

faq.question: Does it replace a wedding planner?
faq.answer: No — it's for organising yourself. It won't run your wedding day, but it handles guests, budget and tables better than spreadsheets and sticky notes.

faq.question: Does it work on my phone?
faq.answer: Yes, in the browser — nothing to install. Phone, tablet and desktop, same account.

Handbook.intro: Module-by-module guide — only features available in the app. Open from the bottom-left icon or Account tab.

overview.title: Introduction
overview.summary: Suggested workflow: guests and budget first, then tasks, seating, portal, day timeline and vendors.

1.title: Handbook icon
1.body: On every dashboard screen — bottom left. Opens this guide (on the current module it scrolls to the matching section).

2.title: Table of contents
2.body: Pick a module on the left (on mobile: expand Table of contents) — Guests, Budget, Tasks, etc.

3.title: Steps in each section
3.body: Each module has a short summary and numbered steps — what to click in the menu and forms.

4.title: Go to module
4.body: At the bottom of a section, Go to module → opens that tab in the app.

guests.title: Guests and RSVP
guests.summary: Guest list for catering, seating and invitations. Card or table view; Excel import; configurable RSVP form.

1.title: Open Guests
1.body: Choose Guests in the menu. RSVP summary appears at the top after first responses.

2.title: Add or import
2.body: Add guest (gold button) or Import guests — download the Excel template, fill First and Last name columns, upload and click Import from CSV.

3.title: RSVP and guest link
3.body: RSVP configuration — which fields guests see. On the card: Generate link, copy the URL or download QR and share it with the guest.

4.title: Status and edit
4.body: Edit the guest card: name, phone, email, notes. Set RSVP status manually or it updates when the guest submits the form. Table view — edit many rows at once.

budget.title: Budget
budget.summary: Target wedding budget (edit on dashboard) plus line items with planned and spent amounts. Dashboard chart shows usage.

2.title: Target budget
2.body: On Dashboard click Edit your wedding, set Target budget and save. That alone marks the budget plan step as started.

3.title: Add line item
3.body: In Budget: Add item — name, category, planned amount, optional spent amount and status (planned / paid).

4.title: Track spending
4.body: After each payment update the spent column. Table footer shows totals; dashboard shows the chart and overspend alert.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.summary: Checklist: Board (status columns) or Timeline. Add tasks manually; optional Generate AI task plan.

2.title: Add a task
2.body: Click + Add — fill title, due date, priority, category, description. Save task adds it to the list.

3.title: AI task plan (optional)
3.body: Generate AI task plan — short questionnaire about your wedding. Requires working AI API on the server (otherwise you will see an error).

4.title: Board and filters
4.body: Tabs Board / Timeline. On the board drag tasks between columns. Search and category/role filters narrow the list.

seating.title: Seating plan
seating.summary: Seating configurator + Assign guests (AI), then table list with drag-and-drop and three PDF exports.

1.title: Guests first
1.body: Under Guests build your list. When editing a guest you can set Place card text — AI uses it when seating.

2.title: AI seating
2.body: Under Seating plan: set Number of tables and Seats per table, click Assign guests (AI). Wait for completion — the list refreshes.

3.title: Table list
3.body: Table list tab: drag guests between tables (⋮⋮ handle). Add new table for a single extra table.

4.title: PDF and layout
4.body: Download place cards PDF, guest list by table, floor layout print. Layout tab — visual floor plan.

portal.title: Guest portal
portal.summary: Public wedding page (custom URL). Guest book section collects messages after the page is live.

2.title: Enable the page
2.body: Check Enable guest page, enter Page address (slug). Click Save configuration — the link appears below the form.

3.title: Content
3.body: Fill message for guests, dress code, ceremony and reception locations and Google Maps links.

4.title: Share the link
4.body: Copy the public page link and share it with guests. The per-guest RSVP link from Guests (with portal on) leads to that page with the confirmation form.

day.title: Organization
day.summary: Wedding day timeline and menu courses. Download PDF for schedule and menu.

2.title: Day timeline
2.body: Add programme items with time, title, description and location. Edit or delete with row actions.

3.title: Menu
3.body: In the wedding menu section add courses (e.g. appetizer, main, cake) with a short description.

4.title: PDF and contacts
4.body: Download PDF – day schedule and Download PDF – menu. Vendor phone numbers live under Vendors.

vendors.title: Vendors
vendors.summary: Contacts for venue, photo, DJ, etc. Documents (contracts, invoices) and automatic Vendor panel link after you add an entry.

2.title: Add entry
2.body: Add vendor — name, category, phone, email, website, notes. Save the form.

3.title: Documents
3.body: On the card: Manage documents — upload contracts and invoices (counters update on the card).

4.title: Vendor panel
4.body: After save the card shows Vendor panel — copy icon sends the link. Info icon previews their panel data.

Editorial.metaTitle: Wedding Board Editorial — who writes our guides
Editorial.metaDescription: Meet the Wedding Board editorial team: how we write wedding guides, what sources we use, and how editorial expertise meets planning tools.
Editorial.title: Wedding Board Editorial
Editorial.lead: The Wedding Board journal is built for couples planning a wedding with clarity, calm and respect for real budgets.
Editorial.body1: Editorial content is produced by the Wedding Board team, informed by wedding planners, couple feedback and anonymised patterns from the app: timelines, budgets, guest lists and seating. Every article is reviewed for relevance to current wedding planning practice.
Editorial.body2: We do not publish sponsored content without disclosure. When an article references Wedding Board features, we say so openly — the guide should remain useful even without an account.
principles: Practical over trendy — guides should support decisions, not just Pinterest inspiration.
Real-world context — timelines, costs and vendor workflows that reflect how couples plan today.
Freshness — seasonal and numeric articles (budget, trends) are reviewed regularly.
Transparency — clear CTAs to the app; no hidden limitations.
Plain language — elegant, accessible copy without industry jargon.
